study_identification_part.si_4_title: A neuroimaging measure to capture heterogeneous patterns of atrophy in Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: This study used a pre-trained normative model from Rutherford et al. (2022) based on 58,836 participants from 82 sites. For the current study, data were collected from two sites: (1) University College London (UCL) - a single-site cohort with PD (n=108), DLB (n=36), and controls (n=38); (2) NACC ADRC '8361' site - DLB (n=25) and controls (n=127). The NACC dataset is from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center database.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Rutherford and colleagues modelled normative lifespan curves for cortical thicknesses across 148 regions (Destrieux parcellation) and subcortical volumes derived from Freesurfer using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression with age and sex as covariates, and accounting for site differences. Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites." ... "The first site at University College London (UCL), included 108 participants with PD, 36 with DLB and 38 controls... The second site was the pseudoanonymised Alzheimer's Disease Research Center (ADRC) '8361' which contributes data to the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) database, and included 25 participants with DLB and 127 controls."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The pre-trained normative model from Rutherford et al. (2022) served as the reference model. Control data from UCL (n=38) and NACC (n=127) sites were used to recalibrate the reference normative model using an adapted transfer learning approach to account for site/scanner differences. PD and DLB patients from both sites were then evaluated against the recalibrated model.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The reference normative model was recalibrated to the study datasets with an adapted transfer learning approach. This involved inputting control data from our two study sites into the reference normative model to generate stable parameters for cortical thicknesses and subcortical volumes, to account for residual differences in data distributions, caused by factors such as scanner differences. Z-scores were then generated for each individual with DLB or PD, per region, relative to the recalibrated reference values."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: This study applied a pre-trained normative model from Rutherford et al. (2022) that was built on 58,836 healthy controls from 82 sites. For the current study, the model was recalibrated using 165 controls (UCL: 38, NACC: 127) via transfer learning to account for site differences. The 165 controls were used specifically for recalibration, not for building the original normative model.
